name: TabletClass Math
line: TabletClass Math teaches by video, chapter by chapter. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs TabletClass Math: TabletClass teaches by video, chapter by chapter. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: TabletClass Math teaches each topic in a teacher-led video, then gives a printable worksheet, with a quiz at the end of each chapter, in a set order [1][3]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything hangs off the problem in front of the learner: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In TabletClass Math the unit is the topic lesson: a lesson video and Example Set videos, and a printable worksheet [3]. In an online psychology course for adults, students who did more interactive activities learned more than students who watched more video or read more pages. The authors call the data correlational [11].

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level in that part of math and sets the next problem. In TabletClass Math a downloadable placement test helps a family choose a course, at least for Algebra 1 [6]. After that, assessment comes at the end of a chapter: an online quiz, and chapter tests and a final exam that the adult grades [3][4].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. Answers are checked exactly, and the adult grades nothing. In TabletClass Math the learner checks a worksheet against the answer key or a solution video, and the adult grades the chapter tests and the final exam and works out the course grade from supplied directions [3][4].

reasons.title: Moving on, and going back
reasons.body: In AMP a skill counts when the learner gets it right without help, more than once. Repeated misses send practice back to what the skill builds on. In TabletClass Math a learner moves on by finishing chapters in a set order [3]. For earlier math, a family can choose Foundations Math, which the site describes as elementary and middle school review [1].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. TabletClass Math practice follows the chapter: each worksheet covers its topic's example sets, and a quiz closes the chapter [3]. We found no scheduled review of earlier chapters in its course materials, only a mention of review sections in the Geometry course description [3]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [10].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math and runs from counting through precalculus in one program. A learner further along in geometry than in fractions gets work at both levels. TabletClass Math is six separate courses, from Foundations Math through Pre-Calculus [1]. A learner chooses a course, and that course sets the level for every topic in it.

rows.range: Six courses: Foundations Math (elementary and middle school review), Pre-Algebra, Algebra 1, Geometry, Algebra 2 and Pre-Calculus [1].
rows.start: The family picks a course. A downloadable placement test helps, at least for Algebra 1 [6].
rows.teaching: Before practice: a teacher-led lesson video and worked-example videos for each topic, plus printable chapter notes [1][3].
rows.next: The next lesson in the chapter, in a set order, the same for every learner [3].
rows.mastery: Finishing chapters. The adult grades chapter tests and a final exam [3][4].
rows.review: No scheduled review of earlier chapters found in its course materials; the Geometry description mentions review sections [3].
rows.print: Printable worksheets with answer keys, and chapter notes, the same for every learner [3].
rows.adult: Picks the course, grades chapter tests and the final exam, and works out the course grade from supplied directions [4].
rows.reports: Online chapter quizzes scored automatically [3]. A guidebook for a portfolio record [4].
rows.evidence: No outcome study found on its site; its testimonials are self-reported [7]. We found no entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse [8][9].

theirs: TabletClass Math is an online math course from TabletClass.com, LLC, at tcmathacademy.com [1]. The site describes its instruction as 100% teacher-led. Its founder, John Zimmerman, teaches the lessons. He lists a math degree, a master's in educational technology, certification to teach middle and high school math, and more than 25 years in the classroom [1][2]. This page is about its homeschool courses.

Each topic has a lesson video and Example Set videos with step-by-step solutions. The learner works a printable worksheet, checks it against the answer key or a solution video, and takes an online quiz at the end of each chapter [3]. A course is planned for about an hour a day, five days a week, over seven to ten months [5]. A Parent Portal adds chapter tests, answer keys, a final exam, a pacing guide and grading directions [4].
credit: One certified math teacher explains every lesson on video, with worked-example videos for each topic [2][3].
Named courses, such as Geometry and Algebra 2, with chapter tests and a final exam [1][4].

theirs: We found no outcome study of TabletClass Math on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [8][9]. Its testimonials page lists self-reported results on the SAT, the GED, placement tests and course grades, with no sample size and no comparison group [7].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on a test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks; the trial meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, though the test was the researchers' own [10]. In an online psychology course for adults, students who did more interactive activities learned more than students who watched more video or read more pages. The authors call the data correlational [11]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: Your child learns best from one teacher explaining each lesson on video before practice.
amp: You want practice to start with a problem, with the hint, lesson and worked answer at hand.
You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want every answer checked and explained, with nothing for you to grade.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your child is at different levels in different parts of math.

questions.question: How is AMP different from TabletClass Math?
questions.answer: TabletClass Math teaches each topic on video, then gives a worksheet, with a quiz at the end of each chapter, in a set order [3]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does TabletClass Math work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of it on its site, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [8][9]. Its testimonials are self-reported, with no comparison group [7].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. They are separate programs. A learner can keep watching TabletClass lessons, and AMP places them from their first answers.
